note: Tattva generated-UI catalog. A model may only use these components. The host owns all styling.
specFormat: { root: string, nodes: { id: string, type: string, props?: object, children?: string[] }[], done?: boolean }

components.description: A container that lays its children out in a column or a grid.
components.whenToUse: Use it to put several parts together under an optional heading. Keep it to one level of nesting.

props.name: title
props.description: Optional heading above the group.

props.name: layout
props.description: stack puts children in one column. grid puts them side by side when there is room. Default stack.

components.description: A short paragraph of plain text.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a sentence or two of explanation. Do not use it for long answers; reply in text instead.

props.name: text
props.description: The words to show. Plain text only.

props.name: tone
props.description: muted is for small side notes. Default normal.

components.description: A highlighted note with a short title and a sentence of detail.
components.whenToUse: Use it for one thing the person should notice: a result, a warning or a tip. Only use warning when a person has to act.

props.name: tone
props.description: info, success, warning or danger. Default info.

props.name: title
props.description: Short heading.

props.name: text
props.description: The note itself.

components.description: One headline number with a label and an optional change.
components.whenToUse: Use it for the two to four numbers that answer the question, such as orders this week. Put them in a grid Group.

props.name: label
props.description: What the number measures, in sentence case.

props.name: value
props.description: The number, already formatted, for example "1,240" or "$4.2K".

props.name: delta
props.description: Change since before.
props.shape: { text: string (for example "+4.2%"), direction: "up" | "down" | "flat", versus?: string }

props.name: goodDirection
props.description: Which way counts as better. Default up.

props.name: detail
props.description: A small line under the number.

components.description: A line chart of one to five series over a list of labels such as days.
components.whenToUse: Use it to show how something changed over time. For comparing categories use BarChart.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: A name that says what the chart shows, for example "Orders per day".

props.name: x
props.description: Labels along the bottom.

props.name: series
props.description: The lines.
props.shape: { id: string, label: string, data: (number | null)[] }[] with one value per label

props.name: unit
props.description: Unit word read aloud after each value, for example "orders".

components.description: A bar chart that compares categories.
components.whenToUse: Use it to compare a handful of categories, such as sales by product. Keep it under about ten bars.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: A name that says what the chart shows, for example "Orders by product".

props.name: data
props.description: The bars, in order.
props.shape: { label: string, value: number (zero or more) }[]

props.name: orientation
props.description: Default horizontal.

props.name: measure
props.description: Name of what is measured, for example "Orders".

props.name: unit
props.description: Unit word read aloud after each value.

props.name: highlight
props.description: Label of one bar to emphasize.

components.description: A table of rows and columns.
components.whenToUse: Use it when the person needs exact values or many attributes. For two or three numbers use StatTile instead.

props.name: caption
props.description: Says what the table holds, for example "Orders this week by day".

props.name: columns
props.description: Column definitions in order. The first column is the row header.
props.shape: { key: string, header: string, numeric?: boolean }[]

props.name: rows
props.description: One object per row, keyed by column key.

components.description: A numbered list of the web pages an answer is based on.
components.whenToUse: Use it under a summary or claim so the person can check where it came from. Only list pages you really used.

props.name: sources
props.description: The pages.
props.shape: { title: string, url: string (https only), domain?: string, snippet?: string }[]

components.description: A short written summary with an AI label, optional extra detail and sources.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a short overview of something that was looked up or worked out. Add sources when the content is factual.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading. Default Overview.

props.name: text
props.description: The summary, plain text.

props.name: detail
props.description: Longer detail the person can open.

props.name: sources
props.description: Pages the summary is based on.

components.description: A plan with numbered steps that the person can approve or ask to change.
components.whenToUse: Use it before doing work with several steps. Set confirm to true when approving starts something that is hard to undo.

props.name: title
props.description: Name of the plan.

props.name: steps
props.description: Steps in order.
props.shape: { id: string, title: string, description?: string }[]

props.name: estimate
props.description: Time or cost, for example "About 6 minutes".

props.name: confirm
props.description: Set to true when pressing this does something that is hard to undo, such as sending, buying or deleting. The person is asked to confirm first.

props.name: consequence
props.description: One plain sentence saying what will happen if the person confirms, for example "This emails 12 customers."

components.description: A small form of choices and numbers with an Apply button.
components.whenToUse: Use it when the person should set a few options before you continue, such as size or style. Never invent other input types.

props.name: title
props.description: Name of the panel.

props.name: parameters
props.description: The controls, in order.
props.shape: { id: string, label: string, kind: "segmented" | "presets" | "number", options?: { value: string, label: string }[], min?: number, max?: number, step?: number, unit?: string, default?: string | number }[]

props.name: submitLabel
props.description: Text of the button. Default Apply.

props.name: confirm
props.description: Set to true when pressing this does something that is hard to undo, such as sending, buying or deleting. The person is asked to confirm first.

props.name: consequence
props.description: One plain sentence saying what will happen if the person confirms, for example "This emails 12 customers."

components.description: A set of options the person picks one from.
components.whenToUse: Use it to offer two to eight alternatives, such as draft titles. Each option needs a label.

props.name: title
props.description: Question above the options, for example "Pick a title".

props.name: variants
props.description: The options.
props.shape: { id: string, label: string, text?: string }[]

props.name: confirm
props.description: Set to true when pressing this does something that is hard to undo, such as sending, buying or deleting. The person is asked to confirm first.

props.name: consequence
props.description: One plain sentence saying what will happen if the person confirms, for example "This emails 12 customers."

components.description: A list of tasks with a short status next to each.
components.whenToUse: Use it to show progress on a few steps. Mark an item attention only when a person has to act.

props.name: items
props.description: The tasks.
props.shape: { id: string, title: string, status?: string, attention?: boolean }[]

props.name: doneSummary
props.description: One line for work that is finished, for example "3 steps done".

components.description: Shows how sure the answer is: low, medium or high.
components.whenToUse: Use it next to a claim you are not fully sure about. Do not use it to decorate answers you are sure of.

props.name: level
props.description: How sure you are.

components.description: A small label such as a status.
components.whenToUse: Use it for one or two words, like "Shipped" or "Late". Do not use it for sentences.

props.name: text
props.description: One or two words.

props.name: tone
props.description: Default neutral. Use warning only when a person has to act.

components.description: A message for when there is nothing to show, with a reason and a next step.
components.whenToUse: Use it when a search or list came back empty or something could not be loaded. Say why, and what to try.

props.name: variant
props.description: Sets the picture and default words. Default no-results.

props.name: title
props.description: What happened.

props.name: text
props.description: The next step, in one sentence.

components.description: A button that sends the person's choice back to you.
components.whenToUse: Use it for one clear next step. Use at most two buttons together. Set confirm to true for anything hard to undo.

props.name: label
props.description: What the button does, as a short verb phrase, for example "Send reminders".

props.name: variant
props.description: Default primary. danger always asks the person to confirm.

props.name: value
props.description: A word you will recognise when the press comes back to you. Defaults to the label.

props.name: confirm
props.description: Set to true when pressing this does something that is hard to undo, such as sending, buying or deleting. The person is asked to confirm first.

props.name: consequence
props.description: One plain sentence saying what will happen if the person confirms, for example "This emails 12 customers."
